book.title: 1934: Caught in the Crossroads
book.genre: Historical Adventure · Book 1 of Echoes of Lost Worlds
book.tagline: March 1934. The True Cross has been lost since the Crusades. It's about to resurface at the worst possible time.
description: Railway work in Yugoslavia uncovers a sealed basement: Ottoman soldiers trapped since the Siege of Vienna, and a Grand Vizier's campaign inventory lost for two and a half centuries. One item on it doesn't belong.

At the unveiling in Ljubljana's museum, men in brown shirts steal the ledger in front of a room full of scholars. A relic, a Nazi thief, a trail across Europe: a perfect job for a famous action archaeologist.

Unfortunately, he isn't available. What we have instead is Fitz, a security chief recalled from his vacation by a telegram that explains nothing; his sister Liz, an actress who can read a room in seconds and jump to the wrong conclusion just as fast; Milan, who dug the thing up and would very much like to go back to not being involved; and Lotte, a German museum worker fired for speaking her mind, who came to meet a resistance contact and arrived too late.

Between them they have a cane, a stage voice, a trowel and a talent for locks. Against them they have Albert Bösmann, a Nazi colonel who doesn't believe in relics, only in what they're worth to the men who do. Also passports, police statements, and an employer who wants a progress report within a week.

The trail runs from an excavation on the Drava to a chapel in a Vienna still under curfew after a civil war, then the Orient Express, a church in Bucharest, and a monastery on an island in Romania. Somewhere along it, a Wallachian prince's secret has waited since 1683.
It is 1934, and the worst still feels avoidable. Real places, real politics, and a lot of making it up as they go.
Book 1 of Echoes of Lost Worlds. A complete adventure: each book follows a new relic through a new year on the road to war.
Content: action violence, no on-page deaths. No sex. Mild language.
